description: Creator-settable dial bounds on MsgUserRequestGuardians, pinned across implementations. The chain asserts these through ValidateBasic AND the keeper's equivalent check (x/secrets/keeper/dial_vectors_test.go); the TypeScript SDK asserts them through its DIALS descriptor table (dials.test.ts). A client that offers a value the chain rejects, or refuses one the chain accepts, fails its own suite. Two timing values are NOT dials: the commit window is the protocol constant CommitTimeoutBlocks (50), which is why the reveal-offset floor is the constant 100 (commit window + 50-block buffer); and the reveal window's length is derived from the offset, pinned separately under reveal_window_derivation. The offset ceiling already carries the longest window the derivation can return, so reveal_end_block lands inside the horizon for every offset that passes and there is no separate horizon check for a client to mirror.

reveal_start_offset_blocks.rule: min = CommitTimeoutBlocks (50) + 50 buffer. max = MaxRevealHorizon (5256000) - RevealWindowCeiling (7200): the furthest opening whose derived window still closes inside the horizon. Both constants, not derived from a creator input.

reveal_window_derivation.description: The reveal window is derived from the hold — the interval over which a secret's guardians are unobserved, from commit_deadline to the window opening. Normative in exactly this integer form: multiplication before division, truncating throughout, integer square root. A float sqrt is not an acceptable substitute; its rounding is not guaranteed identical across architectures and this value fixes a settlement height. Every case below is exact, including both knees.
reveal_window_derivation.formula: hold = reveal_start_offset - CommitTimeoutBlocks; hold <= ramp_start -> window_floor; hold >= ramp_end -> window_ceiling; otherwise window_floor + isqrt((hold - ramp_start) * rise * rise / span)

cases.reason: one block below the ramp: still the floor
ramp start, exact: the last hold on the floor
one block into the ramp: leaves the floor
one block below the ramp end: one block below the ceiling
ramp end, exact: the argument reduces to rise squared, so isqrt returns rise exactly
one block past the ramp end: clamped
the longest possible hold, at the offset ceiling: clamped

cases.name: band exactly at the gap bound
widest legal band below the ceiling
offset exactly at the ceiling, window closing on the horizon
cases.reason: offset 5248800 + derived window 7200 = 5256000, exactly the horizon

cases.name: offset exactly at the reveal-offset floor
band width equals threshold, violating the strict gap bound
reveal offset one block below the floor
cases.reason: start_offset < 100 (the fixed commit window plus the buffer)

cases.name: offset one block above the ceiling
cases.reason: one block past the offset ceiling, so the derived window would close past the horizon
